findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` comes from destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so it is undefined whenever there is no destination calendar. The code then reads `.integration` on it without optional chaining. Any booking with Google Meet as location and no destination calendar throws a TypeError, which breaks booking creation. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Inverted slug condition for organization creation
findings.body: The original code set `slug` only when team billing was disabled (`!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`). The new code sets it only when billing is enabled. Self-hosted instances without billing now create orgs with no slug. Billing instances get a slug set immediately, even though they are meant to store it as `requestedSlug` until payment. This unrelated change reverses the intended behavior.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletes are repeated per reference and only use the first calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring-cancel branch now runs inside the loop over every calendar reference. Each iteration iterates all of the organizer's credentials and deletes only the first `_calendar` reference of each updated booking. With several hosts, the same deletes run N times and the other hosts' events are never deleted. In addition, those deleted results are pushed into `apiDeletes` after they have already been awaited.

findings.title: Only the first old calendar event is deleted when merging on reschedule
findings.body: `updateAllCalendarEvents` now updates all calendar references. When `newBookingId` is set, however, it still deletes only `booking.references.find(...)`, i.e. the first old calendar event. The other hosts' old events are left orphaned in their calendars.

findings.title: updateEvent called with possibly undefined credential
findings.body: If the credential is neither in memory nor found in the DB (or has no app slug), `credential` is undefined and is still passed to `updateEvent`. `updateEvent` then reads `credential.appName` and throws, and the catch block marks every reference as failed. References whose credential is missing should be skipped instead.

findings.title: Organizer email taken from first destination calendar for every host's event
findings.body: The organizer attendee email is always the first (main host's) destination calendar `externalId`. When the event is created in another host's calendar, the organizer email shown is the main host's calendar ID, not the organizer of that copy. This is inconsistent with the per-credential `selectedCalendar` used for the insert.

findings.title: Hangout patch uses undefined calendarId
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` can now be undefined, in which case the insert falls back to "primary". The follow-up `events.patch` that adds the hangout link still passes `selectedCalendar` without that fallback, so the patch request fails. The patch should use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` value.

findings.title: Fallback lookup compares against falsy externalCalendarId
findings.body: This lookup only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then searches for a calendar whose `externalId` equals that falsy value, which never matches. The fallback therefore always yields undefined, which is a regression from using the destination calendar. The same problem exists in `deleteEvent`.
